Uses: Mild to moderate pain such as headache or body pain, and fever.
Key warnings:
• Do not take with any other medicine that also contains paracetamol.
• Never take more than the maximum daily amount on the leaflet: too much can seriously damage the liver.
• Take extra care if you drink alcohol regularly or have liver disease.
Children: Children's products and doses are different: use a children's formulation and check the dose for age and weight.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Generally considered suitable in pregnancy at normal doses, but check with a pharmacist.

Other names (for matching): paracetamol and caffeine; paracetamol caffeine; paracetamol/caffeine; paracetamol + caffeine
Uses: Headache and other mild to moderate pain.
Key warnings:
• Contains paracetamol: do not take with any other paracetamol product.
• Limit tea, coffee and energy drinks: too much caffeine can cause shakiness and poor sleep.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Pain, inflammation (swelling) and fever.
Key warnings:
• Take with or after food.
• Do not combine with other anti-inflammatory painkillers.
• Avoid if you have stomach ulcers, kidney problems or asthma made worse by painkillers.
Children: Children's products and doses are different: check the dose for age and weight.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless a doctor advises.

Uses: Pain and inflammation, for example joint, back or muscle pain.
Key warnings:
• Take with or after food.
• Do not combine with other anti-inflammatory painkillers.
• Avoid with stomach ulcers, heart disease or kidney problems unless a health professional advises.
Children: Not usually for children without a doctor's advice.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless a doctor advises.

Uses: Pain and inflammation, including period pain and joint pain.
Key warnings:
• Take with or after food.
• Do not combine with other anti-inflammatory painkillers.
• Avoid with stomach ulcers or kidney problems unless a health professional advises.
Children: Not usually for children without a doctor's advice.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless a doctor advises.

Uses: Pain and fever in adults. Low doses are sometimes prescribed for the heart.
Key warnings:
• Not for children under 16 unless a doctor says so.
• Do not combine with other anti-inflammatory painkillers.
• Increases bleeding risk; avoid with stomach ulcers.
Children: Do not give to children under 16 unless a doctor prescribes it.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless a doctor advises.

Uses: Moderate to severe pain, only when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Prescription only and controlled: it can cause dependence and is widely misused.
• Causes drowsiness: do not drive, and avoid alcohol.
• Do not take with other medicines that cause drowsiness unless a doctor agrees.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy unless a doctor advises.

Other names (for matching): artemether-lumefantrine; artemether lumefantrine; artemether/lumefantrine; artemether and lumefantrine; artemether + lumefantrine
Uses: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
Key warnings:
• Take with food or milk to help it work.
• Finish the full course even if you feel better.
• Ideally confirm malaria with a test first. Seek care urgently if symptoms are severe or do not improve.
Children: Doses for children depend on weight: check with a pharmacist.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Use in pregnancy only as directed by a health worker.

Other names (for matching): artesunate-amodiaquine; artesunate amodiaquine; artesunate/amodiaquine; artesunate and amodiaquine; amodiaquine and artesunate; amodiaquine artesunate
Uses: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
Key warnings:
• Finish the full course even if you feel better.
• Do not take with other antimalarial treatments.
• Ideally confirm malaria with a test first. Seek care urgently if symptoms are severe or do not improve.
Children: Doses for children depend on age or weight: check with a pharmacist.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Use in pregnancy only as directed by a health worker.

Other names (for matching): dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; dihydroartemisinin piperaquine; dihydroartemisinin/piperaquine; dihydroartemisinin and piperaquine
Uses: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
Key warnings:
• Take on an empty stomach, away from fatty meals (see leaflet).
• Finish the full course even if you feel better.
• Do not take with other antimalarial treatments.
Children: Doses for children depend on weight: check with a pharmacist.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Use in pregnancy only as directed by a health worker.

Other names (for matching): sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine; sulfadoxine pyrimethamine; sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine; sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine
Uses: Mainly used to prevent malaria in pregnancy as part of antenatal care. Not recommended on its own to treat malaria.
Key warnings:
• Use only as directed at antenatal clinic or by a health worker.
• Do not take if allergic to sulfa medicines.
• Stop and seek help urgently if a skin rash appears.
Children: Only as directed by a health worker.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Given in pregnancy only through antenatal care, on the schedule a health worker sets.

Uses: Malaria treatment when prescribed, often for severe malaria in hospital.
Key warnings:
• Only take when prescribed.
• Can cause ringing in the ears, dizziness and low blood sugar.
• Do not combine with other antimalarial treatments unless a doctor directs.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Only when prescribed.

Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not take if you are allergic to penicillin.
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
• Antibiotics do not treat colds or flu.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Other names (for matching): amoxicillin and clavulanic acid; amoxicillin clavulanate; amoxicillin/clavulanic acid; co-amoxiclav; amoxicillin-clavulanate; amoxiclav
Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not take if you are allergic to penicillin.
• Take at the start of a meal to reduce stomach upset.
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Other names (for matching): ampicillin and cloxacillin; ampicillin cloxacillin; ampicillin/cloxacillin; ampicillin + cloxacillin
Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not take if you are allergic to penicillin.
• Usually taken on an empty stomach (see leaflet).
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not take at the same time as antacids, iron, zinc or calcium: they stop it working.
• Stop and seek advice if you get tendon pain or swelling.
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Usually avoided in pregnancy.

Uses: Certain infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not drink alcohol while taking it and for at least 2 days after (see leaflet).
• Can leave a metallic taste.
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Bacterial infections and some malaria prevention, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Swallow with plenty of water while sitting or standing.
• Do not take at the same time as antacids, iron, zinc or calcium.
• Can make skin sensitive to sun.
Children: Not usually for children under 12: it can stain teeth.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy.

Other names (for matching): co-trimoxazole; cotrimoxazole; sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim; sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; sulfamethoxazole trimethoprim
Uses: Certain infections and infection prevention, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Do not take if allergic to sulfa medicines.
• Stop and seek help urgently if a skin rash appears.
• Drink plenty of water.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Keep antacids a few hours apart from it.
• Finish the course prescribed to you, even though it is short.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Bacterial infections, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Tell the pharmacist if you have had a serious allergy to penicillin.
• Take with food.
• Finish the course prescribed to you.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Fungal infections such as vaginal thrush, when advised by a pharmacist or prescribed.
Key warnings: • Interacts with several medicines: tell the pharmacist what else you take.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy unless a doctor advises.

Uses: Fungal skin infections such as ringworm and athlete's foot, and vaginal thrush.
Key warnings:
• For external or vaginal use only: do not swallow.
• Keep using for the time on the leaflet even if it looks better.
Children: Ask a pharmacist before use in young children.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Intestinal worm infections.
Key warnings: • Wash hands and keep nails short to stop reinfection.
Children: Not usually for very young children without advice.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in the first three months of pregnancy.

Uses: Intestinal worm infections.
Key warnings: • Wash hands and keep nails short to stop reinfection.
Children: Not usually for children under 2 without advice.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Avoid in the first three months of pregnancy.

Other names (for matching): oral rehydration salts; oral rehydration salt; ors
Uses: Replacing water and salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.
Key warnings:
• Mix with exactly the amount of clean water the pack says.
• Get help urgently if there is blood in stool, high fever or signs of severe dehydration.
Children: Very important for children with diarrhoea; mix exactly as the pack says.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Generally safe to use; seek care if vomiting or diarrhoea is severe.

Uses: Used with ORS to help children recover from diarrhoea.
Key warnings:
• Can upset the stomach; take after food.
• Keep apart from some antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, doxycycline).
Children: Commonly given to children with diarrhoea alongside ORS; check the dose for age.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Other names (for matching): aluminium hydroxide; magnesium hydroxide; magnesium trisilicate; antacid
Uses: Heartburn and indigestion.
Key warnings: • Keep a gap of a few hours between antacids and other medicines such as some antibiotics and iron.
Children: Ask a pharmacist before giving to children.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Heartburn, acid reflux and stomach ulcers.
Key warnings:
• Take before a meal, usually in the morning.
• See a doctor if you have trouble swallowing, weight loss or black stools.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Short-term relief of diarrhoea in adults.
Key warnings:
• Do not use if there is blood in the stool or a high fever.
• Keep drinking fluids or ORS.
Children: Not for young children: use ORS instead and ask a pharmacist.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Stomach cramps and period cramps.
Key warnings:
• Can cause dry mouth and blurred vision.
• See a doctor if pain is severe or does not go away.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Nausea and vomiting, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Short-term use only.
• Stop and seek advice if you get unusual movements or muscle spasms.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Allergies such as sneezing, runny nose and itchy skin.
Key warnings: • Can occasionally cause drowsiness.
Children: Children's doses are different: check the leaflet.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Allergies such as sneezing, runny nose and itchy skin.
Key warnings: • Can cause drowsiness in some people: avoid alcohol.
Children: Children's doses are different: check the leaflet.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Allergies and itching.
Key warnings:
• Causes drowsiness: do not drive or operate machinery.
• Avoid alcohol.
Children: Children's doses are different; not for very young children.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Allergies, nausea and short-term sleep problems.
Key warnings:
• Causes strong drowsiness: do not drive or operate machinery.
• Avoid alcohol.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Quick relief of asthma and wheezing.
Key warnings:
• If you need it more than usual, see a doctor: your asthma may be getting worse.
• Can cause shakiness and a fast heartbeat.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Keep using as prescribed; uncontrolled asthma is a bigger risk.

Uses: High blood pressure and some heart conditions, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Take every day as prescribed, even if you feel well.
• Can cause ankle swelling.
• Do not stop suddenly without speaking to your doctor.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Type 2 diabetes, when prescribed.
Key warnings:
• Take with or after meals.
• Avoid heavy alcohol drinking.
• Tell your doctor if you become very unwell with vomiting or dehydration.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Ask a pharmacist or doctor before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Uses: Preventing or treating low iron (anaemia).
Key warnings:
• Can darken stool and upset the stomach.
• Keep out of reach of children: iron overdose is dangerous for them.
• Keep apart from antacids and some antibiotics.
Children: Children's doses are different; keep tablets locked away.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Commonly advised in pregnancy: take as directed at antenatal clinic.

Uses: Preventing some birth defects in pregnancy and treating some types of anaemia.
Key warnings: • Take every day as advised.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Recommended before and in early pregnancy: take as directed.

Uses: Vitamin C supplementation.
Key warnings: • High doses can upset the stomach.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Normal doses are generally fine; ask before high doses.

Other names (for matching): vitamin b complex; b complex; vitamin b-complex
Uses: Vitamin B supplementation.
Key warnings: • Can turn urine bright yellow; this is harmless.
Pregnancy / breastfeeding: Normal doses are generally fine; ask a pharmacist.
